title: Beyond the Horizon: New Zealand Bets on AI to Bulletproof Its Supply Chains
summary: New Zealand, a nation heavily reliant on global trade and geographically isolated, faces persistent supply chain vulnerabilities. Emerging AI agents in procurement offer a powerful new tool to enhance resilience and mitigate the impact of future international disruptions.
content:
Recent tumultuous years have hammered home a stark reality for businesses across New Zealand: the next global supply chain shock is never far away. From geopolitical flashpoints to natural disasters and sudden surges in commodity prices, the island nation’s unique position — isolated yet profoundly reliant on international trade — makes its economic lifelines acutely exposed.

Historically, events like major shipping bottlenecks or sudden disruptions in critical routes, such as the Strait of Hormuz, have sent ripples across the globe, impacting everything from oil prices to the availability of consumer goods. For New Zealand, these distant tremors often translate into significant local challenges, demonstrating a pressing need for more robust and agile supply chain management.

It's against this backdrop that a quiet revolution in procurement is taking hold overseas. Intelligent AI agents, autonomous software systems designed to analyze vast datasets, predict demand, and identify risks, are starting to transform how companies source goods and manage logistics. These agents can monitor global events in real-time, forecast potential disruptions, suggest alternative suppliers, and even reroute shipments on the fly, moving beyond reactive fixes to proactive resilience.

For New Zealand specifically, leveraging such technology could be a game-changer. By integrating AI agents into their procurement strategies, Kiwi businesses gain an unprecedented ability to anticipate global shocks, identify vulnerabilities within their own supply networks, and diversify sourcing before crises hit. This isn't just about mitigating damage; it's about building an inherent robustness that protects the nation's economy from the unpredictable currents of global trade, transforming vulnerability into vigilant strength.
keyTakeaways: New Zealand's isolated geography and trade dependence make its supply chains highly vulnerable to global disruptions.
AI agents are transforming international procurement by offering proactive risk management and resilience-building capabilities.
Adopting AI-powered tools can enable New Zealand businesses to anticipate shocks, optimize logistics, and secure alternative supplies, enhancing national economic stability.
author: Ilan Oshri, Professor of Information Systems, Auckland Business School, University of Auckland, Waipapa Taumata Rau

title: SoftBank and ASI Unveil Joint Venture to Supercharge Autonomous Construction
summary: Tech giant SoftBank Group and autonomous vehicle pioneer Autonomous Solutions, Inc. (ASI) have formed a joint venture to accelerate the commercialization of large-scale autonomous construction solutions. This partnership combines SoftBank's significant funding with ASI's 25 years of Mobius® fleet management expertise, aiming to revolutionize infrastructure development with OEM-agnostic, mixed-fleet autonomy.
content:
Imagine a construction site where heavy machinery operates tirelessly, efficiently, and with unparalleled precision, all without a human hand on the controls. That future just took a significant leap closer to reality. In a move set to redefine infrastructure development, SoftBank Group has partnered with Autonomous Solutions, Inc. (ASI) to form a new joint venture, dedicated to pushing autonomous construction to an unprecedented scale.

This isn't just another tech investment; it's a strategic fusion of capital and decades of specialized know-how. SoftBank, renowned for its audacious bets on transformative technologies, brings the financial muscle. ASI, on the other hand, is no newcomer, boasting over 25 years at the forefront of autonomous vehicle software, particularly with its sophisticated Mobius® fleet management platform. This combination promises to accelerate the commercialization of ASI's OEM-agnostic solutions, meaning their autonomy can be integrated across diverse fleets of construction equipment, regardless of manufacturer.

The implications for the construction industry are profound. Autonomous heavy equipment can operate 24/7, dramatically increasing project speeds and reducing operational costs. More critically, it offers a pathway to significantly enhance safety in inherently dangerous environments and address the persistent labor shortages plaguing the sector. From massive public works to new urban developments, this partnership aims to make next-generation infrastructure projects not just faster and cheaper, but also safer.

As our world demands ever-smarter infrastructure, the SoftBank-ASI venture signals a pivotal moment. It's a clear statement that the future of building isn't just digital; it's autonomous, and it's arriving on our construction sites sooner than many might have imagined.
keyTakeaways: SoftBank's significant investment is funding ASI's advanced autonomous construction technology through a new joint venture.
The partnership leverages ASI's 25 years of expertise and its Mobius® platform to deliver OEM-agnostic, mixed-fleet autonomous solutions at scale.
This collaboration is poised to revolutionize the construction industry by boosting efficiency, enhancing safety, and addressing critical labor shortages in infrastructure development.
author: Business Wire
